Independent reproduction, end to end, plus two notes on the patch in #41286.

**End to end.** `create_react_agent` with `ChatOpenAI(streaming=True)`, against a local server that cuts a `write_file` call in the middle of line 17 of a 40-line file. Both `finish_reason: "length"` and a stream that simply ends (no finish reason, no `[DONE]`) give the same result: the tool writes the first 16 lines plus part of line 17, returns success, and the agent answers "Done.". Same with `use_responses_api=True` (`response.incomplete`). With `streaming=False` the tool is not called. On the same server, the OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, Codex CLI and Hermes Agent don't run the cut-off call. Harness and per-run server logs: https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-cutoff-bench

**Two notes for whoever lands the fix**, checked against #41286 at `5e75fa5`:

1. The non-streaming parser uses `json.loads(..., strict=False)`. A strict `json.loads` at finalization marks a complete call whose string contains a raw newline as invalid, so a call that runs without streaming would stop running with streaming.
2. Fixing it in `message_chunk_to_message` covers `invoke()`, but code that sums the chunks itself (`full = full + chunk`, then `full.tool_calls`) still gets the healed arguments. Checking in `init_tool_calls` once `chunk_position == "last"` covers both.

`fix/langchain-core/edge_cases.py` in that repo prints both cases for any build, and `fix/langchain-core/` has a patch that does the check that way, with tests for both. @Kylinny, feel free to use any of it.

issue.title: core: truncated tool-call arguments are parsed leniently after the stream ends, producing a valid-looking tool call

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [x] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

- #39275: same report, auto-closed for submission format, not reviewed on the merits.
- #38682 and #35743 (empty-args handling during streaming): adjacent but different.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import generate_from_stream
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessageChunk
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGenerationChunk

chunks = [
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": "edit_document", "args": "", "id": "call_1", "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": None, "args": '{"operation": "replace", "blocks": [{"type": "hea',
         "id": None, "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
]
msg = generate_from_stream(iter(chunks)).generations[0].message
print(msg.tool_calls)
# [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, ...}]
print(msg.invalid_tool_calls)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

No error or stack trace. The bug is silent: a tool call whose arguments were cut off by the end of the stream comes out as a valid-looking tool call.

Running the reproduction above prints:

```python
  msg.tool_calls
  [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, 'id': 'call_1', 'type': 'tool_call'}]

  msg.invalid_tool_calls
  []
```
Expected: the truncated arguments land in invalid_tool_calls (raw string preserved) and tool_calls is empty.

### Description

`AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls` parses every tool-call chunk's `args` with `parse_partial_json`. That's right while a stream is in flight. But it's also used for the final aggregated message: both the `chunk_position="last"` chunk and the message that `generate_from_stream` builds for `invoke()` / `ainvoke()` with `streaming=True`.

If a stream ends partway through a tool call's arguments, partial parsing closes the open strings and brackets and returns a well-formed dict:
- the call lands in `tool_calls`;
- `invalid_tool_calls` stays empty;
- the tool runs with half of its input.

Streams end early more often than you'd think:
- a provider or proxy closes the connection;
- a gateway that reports a dropped upstream with `finish_reason: "stop"` (we saw this with an LLM proxy);
- a timeout in an intermediary.

Our concrete case: half of a document-edit payload was applied as a complete edit.

### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Darwin
> OS Version:  Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:06:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
> Python Version:  3.11.15 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:46:51) [Clang 22.1.3 ]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.6.12
> langsmith: 0.14.9
> langchain_protocol: 0.0.18
> langchain_tests: 1.1.9

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

issue.title: fix(core): truncated tool-call arguments land in invalid_tool_calls on finalized messages

labels.name: fix
labels.description: For PRs that implement a fix

issue.body:
## What

`message_chunk_to_message` re-derives tool calls with strict JSON instead of inheriting the chunk validator's lenient parse. Truncated or malformed tool-call arguments now land in `invalid_tool_calls` (raw string preserved) on the finalized message; previously `parse_partial_json` healed them into a valid-looking call with half an input.

## Why

While a stream is in flight, lenient parsing is what you want - partial arguments should be visible. But the same lenient parse ran at the finalization boundary, so a stream that ended mid-arguments produced a `tool_calls` entry and an empty `invalid_tool_calls`. The tool then runs with half its input, silently. We hit this behind a proxy that reported a dropped upstream as `finish_reason: "stop"`.

The non-streaming path (`default_tool_parser`) already behaves this way - `json.loads` or invalid - so this makes streaming and non-streaming agree.

## Testing

- New regression test: truncated args end in `invalid_tool_calls`, complete args still parse, in-flight chunks keep the lenient behavior.
- Updated the existing `test_message_chunk_to_message` expectation: the `args='{"b": '` chunk was previously healed to `{}`; it is now invalid, which is the behavior change this fix intends.
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/test_messages.py` -> 57 passed. ruff check + format clean.

Fixes #41285
